html:
The great slave uprising that broke out in the French colony of Saint-Domingue in August 1791 and ended with the independent state of Haiti in 1804. It is the only slave revolt in history that founded a state.

Saint-Domingue was then the richest colony in the world, rich in sugar and coffee. About half a million enslaved Africans worked there under brutal conditions, far outnumbering the white planters and the free people of colour.

The main steps:

  • August 1791: after a Vodou ceremony at Bois Caïman, linked with the leader Dutty Boukman, enslaved people on the northern plain rose up and burned the plantations.
  • 1793 to 1794: French officials freed the enslaved, and the French Republic abolished slavery in all its colonies.
  • Toussaint Louverture took control of the colony by 1801.
  • 1802 to 1803: Napoleon sent an army to restore the old order; disease and Dessalines's forces destroyed it.

The defeat helped persuade Napoleon to sell Louisiana to the United States. Slaveholders across the Americas feared Haiti's example, and France forced the new state to pay a heavy indemnity from 1825.
sum: The great slave uprising that broke out in the French colony of Saint-Domingue in August 1791 and ended with the independent state of Haiti in 1804. It is the only slave revolt in history that founded a state.
